newsitem.title: ESTONIA: FOREKS AIMS FOR TEN PCT MARKET SHARE.
newsitem.headline: FOREKS AIMS FOR TEN PCT MARKET SHARE.

text.p: Forekspank plans to increase its share of the Estonian banking market from seven percent to eight at the end of this year and to ten percent at the end of 1998, the bank's chairman, Ivar Lukk, said on Wednesday.
"We plan to grow faster than our competitors," Lukk told a meeting of shareholders.
Forekspank's market share grew from 6.3 percent at the beginning of the year to seven percent in March, Lukk said.
"Our target is not too optimistic," he added.
Lukk also said that the bank plans to expand its activities oiuside of Estonia.
The bank opened a representative office in Moscow in March.
"The bank is very seriously researching if it is sensible, taking into account our risk standards, to go into commercial banking there," Lukk said.
Forekspank also plans to open a South-Estonian centre office later this month and an office in Parnu next year.
"Forekspank will have four strong regional centres in the future - in Tallinn, Narva, Parnu and Tartu," Lukk said.
Forekspank group's net profit profit estimate for 1997 is 75 million kroons and 72 million kroons for the bank. The bank had a net profit of 46.6 million kroons last year.
The bank estimates its balance sheet to grow to 2.6 billion kroons and its loan portfolio to 1.1 billion kroons.
"The bank will probably revise the estimates in the second half of the year," Raivo Erik, the bank's finance director, said.
"The bank will also very seriously consider proposing a stock dividend issue at the next shareholders' annual meeting," Lukk said.
The bank did not issue stock dividends this year because of changes made to statues at Wednesday's shareholders meeting.
